checked_sources.result: Direct open attempted; web fetch timed out. Do not count this attempt as successful source verification.

checked_sources.evidence: Opened current full German Basic Law at the official Ministry of Justice/Federal Office of Justice site; Article 22(2) states the federal flag is black-red-gold. This verified alternate can replace the timed-out article-specific link.
Opened the German flag order, section I.1: equal-width transverse stripes, black above, red middle, gold below, cloth height:length 3:5.

Opened Bundestag history page: origins cannot be identified with certainty; describes unity/freedom context, 1848 declaration by the Frankfurt Federal Diet and National Assembly, and the 1949 Parliamentary Council decision.

minimal_corrections: Replace source_links URL https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gg/art_22.html with the successfully opened official full-text Basic Law URL https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gg/BJNR000010949.html. No body change is needed.

checked_sources.evidence: Actually opened the Quirinale-hosted Constitution PDF; Article 12 gives green, white and red in three equal vertical bands.

Actually opened the Presidency's history page; it documents the Cispadane Republic decree at Reggio Emilia on 7 January 1797 and the provisional 19 June 1946 flag, 24 March 1947 confirmation, and insertion into Article 12.
Actually opened the image linked by the Quirinale history page; it depicts the current green-white-red vertical tricolour and supports the article's staff-to-fly reading.

Actually opened the BOE consolidated Constitution page (text extraction timed out when reopening specific lines); the officially hosted consolidated Constitution PDF was also opened and verified Article 4: red-yellow-red horizontal bands, yellow twice each red band's width, and autonomous-community flags may be used alongside the Spanish flag.
Actually opened BOE's consolidated Constitution PDF and located Article 4.1–4.2. The text matches the article's stripe order, 1:2:1 ratio and regional-flag qualification.

Actually opened La Moncloa's state-flag history page. It attributes the present flag's origin to Charles III; explains the white-ensign identification problem at sea; and says the 1785 decree selected separate designs for the navy and merchant fleet, with later broader use.

Answers are correct.

limitations: The German article-specific Basic Law URL timed out on direct open; its claim was verified from the successfully opened current official full-text Basic Law and Bundestag source. Recommend replacing the failed URL before acceptance.
The Spanish BOE HTML page opened, but a later line extraction timed out; the opened current consolidated BOE PDF verified the corresponding Article 4 text.
